newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: New bid seen made for Aida, MD steps down.
newsitem.headline: New bid seen made for Aida, MD steps down.

text.p: Lew Geffen, key shareholder in South African real estate firm Lew Geffen Estates, said on Wednesday that a consortium led by him will not buy a controlling stake in or take management control of Aida Holdings Ltd.

Geffen said that he understood that a counter offer to acquire a controlling interest in Aida would be made which would bring value to the beneficiaries of the Aida Geffen Trust which currently own the real estate business.
Geffen, who had been appointed managing director of Aida, said he would step down from this position and pursue plans to develop Lew Geffen Estates into a significant property finance operation.

"Lew Geffen Estates will now be developed as a property financial group in its own right with a view to seeking a listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange at a suitable future date," a statement said on Wednesday.

Aida said last month that Geffen's 85 cent-a-share offer for 51 percent of the firm, equivalent to an offer of 6.4 million rand, had lapsed but that fresh negotiations were under way between the Aida Family Trust, Aida Geffen and Geffen to enable the purchase of a controlling interest.
Geffen said on Wednesday that the parties had agreed that there was "little point" in Geffen and his partners paying over six million rand into the trust.
